test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 29 Jun, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that “There shall be a High Court for each state”?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 214**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 214** of the Indian Constitution states that "There shall be a High Court for each state."
 
• Each state in India has its own High Court which is the principal civil court of original jurisdiction in the state.
 
• The High Court primarily deals with cases involving civil, criminal, and constitutional law.
 
• The High Courts have the power to issue writs for enforcing fundamental rights and for any other purpose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **High Courts** play a crucial role in the Indian judiciary system, serving as the intermediate appellate courts between the lower courts and the Supreme Court of India.
